title: test_mount_starbook_simulator: starbook_firmware_thresholds_select_commands is load-sensitive
description: starbook_firmware_thresholds_select_commands failed intermittently when other suites ran on the same machine and passed in sequential runs (28/28 in the recorded run of 2026-11-20). Find the timing assumption and make the case independent of machine load.

outcome.summary: Pass, no defects. The root cause is confirmed. In indigo_drivers/mount_starbook/indigo_mount_starbook.driver:533-544, on_timer runs every 0.5 s and republishes MOUNT_UTC_TIME as OK whenever the state is not BUSY. The refusal at :649 is therefore an ALERT update that the next poll replaces. The old wait_for_property_state_after (indigo_test/integration/simulator_test_common.h:390) needed ALERT to still be in the cache when the 100 ms wait loop sampled it, so it was load-sensitive. Independent reproduction on a scratch copy built against the worktree, with a 1 s sleep before the wait: the old wait failed 2/2 at that assertion; the new wait passed 2/2; the unmodified case passed 2/2. The new wait still proves the ALERT came after this request: property_state_revisions[state] stores the global revision of the last update in that state (simulator_test_common.h:238-239), and revision is taken before indigo_change_text_property (test_mount_starbook_simulator.c:998), so an earlier ALERT cannot satisfy it. The /SETTIME count of 0 at :1006 still checks that no command was sent. Driver behaviour: I consider it legitimate and not worth a ticket. MOUNT_UTC_TIME mirrors the mount clock. mount_lx200 (indigo_mount_lx200.c:4080-4089) and mount_ioptron (indigo_mount_ioptron.c:1795-1809) use the same poll pattern. The lx200 (:3481, :5145), nexstar (:793, :1300) and rainbow (:326, :391) suites already wait for refused-UTC ALERTs with wait_for_property_state_seen_after. Clients still receive the ALERT update on the bus. Other waits in the case: GEOGRAPHIC_COORDINATES ALERT (:994), X_STARBOOK_TIMEZONE ALERT (:995) and MOUNT_SET_HOST_TIME ALERT (:1002) are not republished by the poll, so they are stable. The EQUATORIAL waits (:984-985) already use seen_after for BUSY and wait for the steady OK. Out of scope, for the owner only: :524 wait_for_fast_state_after(BUSY) samples a guider BUSY that lasts only 20 ms with a 1 ms loop, which is the same 'current state of a transient state' pattern (

history.text: Building library, starbook driver and suite in the worktree
Running starbook firmware-thresholds case under artificial CPU load
Running full starbook suite under artificial load after the fix

Root cause (test assumption, not a driver defect): indigo_test/integration/test_mount_starbook_simulator.c:1000 waited with wait_for_property_state_after(UTC_TIME, ALERT) for the refused UTC time write on firmware 2.70. The driver's 0.5 s status poll (indigo_mount_starbook.driver on_timer, MOUNT_UTC_TIME block) republishes the mount clock as OK right after the refusal, so ALERT is the current state only until the next poll; a test thread delayed by machine load missed it. Reproduction: the first run of the case on a loaded machine failed at line 1000; deterministic repro by a temporary 1 s delay before that wait failed 3/3 at the same assertion. Fix: wait_for_property_state_seen_after(UTC_TIME, ALERT, revision), the convention the suite already uses for poll-overwritten ALERTs; with the same 1 s delay it passed 3/3. The /SETTIME count stays 0. After the fix: case 10/10 unloaded before fix (baseline flakiness only under external load), full suite 3x 28/28 under 24 busy loops, recorded run 2026-11-20 19:40 28/28 OK. No driver change.

Out of scope, for the owner only: :524 wait_for_fast_state_after(BUSY) samples a guider BUSY that lasts only 20 ms with a 1 ms loop, which is the same 'current state of a transient state' pattern (overwritten by the guider finalizer, not the poll) and can be load-sensitive. :642 and :1066 wait for UTC_TIME OK after a set; they rely on the synchronously published BUSY and the poll's BUSY guard, and only a theoretical race between the poll's state check at .driver:535 and its OK assignment at :539 could end them early. Formatting: tabs, a one-line call and a // comment; the whitespace check passed. The README change is only the ## Testing record line, replaced in place for the mac arm64 simulator configuration. It matches the TEST_SUMMARY.md row (2026-11-20 19:40, 3.0.0.14, 28/28 OK), and 3.0.0.14 matches version = 14 in the .driver. There is no driver change, so no version bump is needed. Nothing else is touched. Not verified: the full suite under load and the recorded 19:40 run itself.
